literal: Missed day without occurring good if [one] does, that [is for] a person living days' path blocking stone.
translation: If one does good without letting a single day go to waste, that virtue will be the stone that blocks their path of future births.
modern: ஒருவன் அறம் செய்யத் தவறிய நாள் ஒன்று கூட ஏற்படாதவாறு தொடர்ந்து நற்செயல்களைச் செய்தால், அந்த அறமே அவனது பிறவி வழியை அடைக்கும் கல்லாக மாறும்.
explanation: This couplet emphasizes the importance of practicing virtue continuously. The phrase 'வீழ்நாள்' refers to a day that falls away or is wasted without doing good. If a person ensures that not a single day passes without performing a virtuous act, that accumulated virtue acts as a powerful barrier. The poet compares this virtue to a stone ('கல்') that firmly blocks the path of living days ('வாழ்நாள் வழி'). While 'வாழ்நாள்' literally means 'days of life', in this context it signifies the endless cycle of rebirths. Thus, relentless virtue is the key to ending worldly suffering.
